items.a: Yes, through institution-approved drives with published eligibility, selection stages, accessibility and data-sharing terms. The platform should preserve auditability and candidate communication.

items.q: Can employers run skill challenges?
items.a: Yes, when the task has a learning purpose, reasonable effort, transparent evaluation and fair intellectual-property terms. Challenges must not replace paid production work.

items.q: Can employers access assessment results?
items.a: Only with explicit candidate consent and only when the specific assessment is valid and lawful for that decision. Developmental career results should not become hidden hiring filters.

items.q: How is candidate data shared?
items.a: Through purpose-limited, role-based access to the minimum data required, with consent records, security controls, retention limits and a way for candidates to exercise their rights.

items.q: Can employers sponsor courses or events?
items.a: Yes, with clear labelling and editorial independence. Sponsorship should expand access or relevance without purchasing favourable recommendations or learner data.

items.q: Can employers provide mentors?
items.a: Yes, after mentor verification, safeguarding training, programme orientation and conflict checks. Employee participation should have defined time and escalation support.

items.q: How does Career Garage improve hiring quality?
items.a: It can improve role awareness, preparedness and evidence through projects and structured profiles. Any claim about hiring efficiency or retention must be supported by verified employer outcomes.

items.q: What analytics do employers receive?
items.a: They may receive funnel, event, challenge and aggregate skill insights relevant to their programme. Sensitive traits, minors’ data and individual assessment results require stronger justification and consent.

items.q: How are employer partnerships monitored?
items.a: Track listing accuracy, response times, participant feedback, selection fairness, compensation, safety incidents and completion. Partners that breach standards should be corrected, suspended or removed.

sections.title: Technology, AI, Data Privacy and Security

items.q: What technology powers Career Garage?
items.a: A secure web and mobile architecture should combine identity, assessment, content, booking, learning, community and analytics services. The final stack should be selected for reliability, accessibility, interoperability and data governance.

items.q: How is AI used?
items.a: AI can support search, summarisation, recommendation drafts, content tagging, translations and risk triage. It should not make unreviewed high-impact decisions, diagnose users or fabricate current career facts.  [R7]

items.q: Does AI make the final career decision?
items.a: No. AI may organise evidence and suggest possibilities, but the learner makes the decision with human guidance and real-world information. The interface must make that limitation visible.  [R7]

items.q: How are AI recommendations checked?
items.a: Use approved source data, rule constraints, human review for high-impact cases, test sets, bias and safety evaluation, logging, incident review and ongoing outcome monitoring.  [R7]

items.q: Can users understand why AI made a recommendation?
items.a: They should see the principal factors, evidence, uncertainty and alternative options in plain language. Proprietary complexity is not an excuse for an unexplained high-impact suggestion.  [R7]

items.q: What happens if the AI is wrong?
items.a: Users need a simple correction and human-review route. Material errors should be traced, corrected, communicated where necessary and used to improve the model or source system.  [R7]

items.q: What data does Career Garage collect?
items.a: Only data needed for the stated service—such as identity and contact details, education profile, assessment responses, activity, bookings and authorised outcome evidence. Every category should appear in a privacy notice and retention schedule.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Why is this data needed?
items.a: Each field must map to a service purpose, legal basis and retention period. Optional personalisation data should be clearly optional, and collection should stop when the purpose can be met without it.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Is student data sold?
items.a: The recommended policy is no. Career Garage should not sell personal data or sensitive assessment profiles; any partner access must be purpose-limited, consented where required and contractually controlled.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Who can access assessment results?
items.a: The learner, authorised guardian where appropriate, assigned qualified professionals and specifically authorised institution users—each through least-privilege, logged access. Employers do not receive results by default.  [R1–R2]

items.q: How long is personal data stored?
items.a: Retention should be purpose- and age-specific, with shorter periods for raw recordings, identity documents and inactive accounts. The public schedule must explain deletion, legal holds and anonymised research data.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Can users delete their data?
items.a: Users should be able to request deletion, subject to lawful exceptions and records needed to protect rights or resolve disputes. The process should state what was deleted, retained and why.  [R1–R2]

items.q: How is data secured?
items.a: Use encryption in transit and at rest, strong authentication, least privilege, secure development, vendor review, backups, monitoring, vulnerability management and an incident-response plan. Security claims should be tested, not assumed.  [R1–R2]

items.q: What happens during a data breach?
items.a: Contain and investigate the incident, protect accounts, preserve evidence, assess harm, notify authorities and affected users as required, remediate causes and document lessons. A named incident team and rehearsal are essential.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Does Career Garage comply with India’s data-protection law?
items.a: The platform must be designed for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the phased Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, including clear notices, valid consent, user rights, child safeguards, grievance handling and processor controls. Formal compliance requires ongoing legal review.  [R1–R2]

items.q: How is children’s data protected?
items.a: Apply age assurance, verifiable parental consent where required, privacy-protective defaults, minimal collection, restricted profiling and messaging, careful vendor access and rapid safety escalation. Commercial design should never exploit children’s data.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Can data be used for research?
items.a: Yes only under a defined protocol with consent or another lawful basis, minimisation, de-identification, access controls, ethics review where appropriate and publication rules that prevent re-identification.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Are third-party tools used?
items.a: Likely yes for hosting, payments, communications or analytics, but every processor requires due diligence, contractual controls, security review, data-location analysis and a public disclosure where relevant.  [R1–R2]

items.q: Is Career Garage free?
items.a: A free foundational tier can provide career information, basic exploration and selected events. Deeper assessment, professional counselling, live programmes and verified services may be paid or institution-sponsored.

items.q: What does the free plan include?
items.a: The final plan should list exact entitlements, but a responsible baseline includes profile creation, selected career-library access, introductory tools and safety-support access—without harvesting data as hidden payment.

items.q: What are the paid plans?
items.a: Use simple plans aligned to outcomes: assessment and report, guidance package, learner journey, institution programme and professional training. Exact inclusions and limits must be visible before purchase.

items.q: How much does an assessment cost?
items.a: Pricing should follow validation, delivery, interpretation and support costs, with regional affordability testing. Until approved, quote only an official current price sheet—not an improvised number during a presentation.

items.q: How much does counselling cost?
items.a: Fees can vary by counsellor level, duration, language and package. Display the total price, taxes, included follow-up and cancellation terms before booking.

items.q: Are there student discounts?
items.a: Yes, through transparent school, need-based, scholarship or campaign programmes with published eligibility. Discounts should not create artificial list prices.

items.q: Are there institutional packages?
items.a: Yes, using cohort, per-learner, annual licence or managed-programme models. Proposals should separate platform access, professional services, events and optional modules.

items.q: Can companies sponsor student access?
items.a: Yes, through CSR, scholarship, community or talent programmes with clear beneficiary criteria, impact reporting and strict limits on data and marketing access.

items.q: What is Career Garage’s revenue model?
items.a: A balanced model can combine B2C guidance, B2B institution programmes, professional training, opportunity and expert services, and sponsored access. Revenue sources must not distort career recommendations.

items.q: Does Career Garage charge employers?
items.a: It may charge for verified listings, programme management, challenges, events or talent services. Charging should never allow an employer to bypass quality or safety review.

items.q: Does Career Garage earn commission on courses?
items.a: It may, if disclosed clearly. Recommendations should use suitability and quality criteria, show alternatives and separate commercial ranking from guidance.

items.q: Does Career Garage charge experts or mentors?
items.a: A transparent platform or service fee may apply to paid engagements; volunteer programmes should not hide participation charges. Payout, cancellation and tax terms must be agreed before activation.

items.q: What is the refund policy?
items.a: The policy should specify eligibility by product, cancellation timing, service consumption, technical failure and statutory rights, with a defined processing timeline and escalation contact.

items.q: How will Career Garage remain affordable?
items.a: Use tiered services, shared institution delivery, low-bandwidth design, scholarships, sponsored seats, group formats and disciplined costs while protecting quality-critical counselling and safety functions.

items.q: Where will Career Garage launch first?
items.a: The recommended approach is a phased India launch, beginning where institutional partners, counsellors, language support and operations are strongest. Bihar, Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh can be priority markets if readiness data confirms the strategy.

items.q: What is the launch timeline?
items.a: Publish a timeline only after product, assessment, legal, safety and service-readiness gates are passed. A credible roadmap separates pilot, limited release, evaluation and scale rather than announcing one symbolic date.

items.q: What is included in the pilot?
items.a: A representative pilot should test onboarding, consent, selected assessments, report interpretation, counselling, at least one action programme, support, safety and outcome measurement—not every future feature.

items.q: How many students are needed for a pilot?
items.a: Choose enough learners to test workflows and important subgroups, not a vanity number. Psychometric validation may require a much larger, separately designed sample than an operational pilot.

items.q: How are pilot institutions selected?
items.a: Select for leadership commitment, learner diversity, device and timetable feasibility, safeguarding readiness, data agreement and willingness to provide honest feedback.

items.q: What infrastructure does an institution need?
items.a: At minimum, a coordinator, secure learner roster, consent process, suitable devices or lab access, stable-enough connectivity, private counselling space and an escalation contact. Low-connectivity alternatives should be planned.

items.q: What support is available during implementation?
items.a: Provide an implementation manager, staff training, learner and parent orientation, technical help, counsellor scheduling, issue escalation and regular progress reviews.

items.q: How long does institutional onboarding take?
items.a: A standard implementation may require several weeks depending on data, consent, calendar and customisation. The proposal should use readiness milestones rather than promise the same date for every institution.

items.q: Who is responsible for student communication?
items.a: Use a joint communication plan: the institution provides trusted local channels and context, while Career Garage supplies approved messages, consent information, schedules and support details.

items.q: How are service complaints handled?
items.a: Offer one visible intake route, acknowledgement and severity-based response targets, independent escalation, documented resolution and trend review. Safety and data complaints must follow specialist protocols.

items.q: What service-level commitments are provided?
items.a: Contracts should define platform availability, support hours, response and restoration targets, session rescheduling, data incident notice and exclusions. Commitments must match actual operating capacity.

items.q: How will Career Garage scale quality?
items.a: Standardise high-risk processes, automate administration, train and supervise practitioners, audit samples, monitor outcomes and expand only when capacity and safeguards meet thresholds.

items.q: How are partners onboarded?
items.a: Verify the organisation and people, complete contracts and data terms, train users, test the workflow, assign owners and approve a limited launch before full access.

items.q: What are the main operational risks?
items.a: Key risks include weak assessment evidence, variable counselling, child-safety failures, outdated information, fake opportunities, data incidents, overclaiming, poor partner delivery and unaffordable support. Each needs an owner, preventive control and response plan.

items.q: How does Career Garage measure student success?
items.a: Measure informed decision quality, completed action plans, career exploration, skill evidence, confidence without overconfidence, applications and transitions. Use baselines and follow-up rather than a single satisfaction score.

items.q: What are the key impact metrics?
items.a: Core metrics can include equitable reach, assessment completion quality, counselling action completion, projects or courses completed, mentorship and internship outcomes, transition progress, wellbeing safeguards and stakeholder satisfaction.

items.q: How quickly can a student see results?
items.a: A learner can gain initial clarity after assessment and counselling, but durable outcomes require weeks or months of action. Present immediate, intermediate and long-term outcomes separately.

items.q: Can Career Garage prove that its recommendations work?
items.a: It should build evidence through validation studies, user comprehension, action completion, comparative pilots and longitudinal outcomes. Until then, it must state evidence honestly and avoid causal claims.

items.q: How are long-term outcomes tracked?
items.a: With consented follow-ups at defined intervals, education and work transitions, portfolio evidence and partner confirmations where appropriate. Attrition and self-report limitations should be reported.

items.q: Can institutions compare cohort outcomes?
items.a: Yes, when definitions, time periods and learner mix are comparable. Dashboards should show context and uncertainty and avoid punitive league tables.

items.q: How is inclusion measured?
items.a: Track access, completion, experience and outcomes by relevant geography, gender, disability, language, income proxy and institution type, using privacy-safe minimum group sizes.

items.q: How is learner satisfaction measured?
items.a: Use short, age-appropriate surveys after key services plus open feedback and complaint data. Ask about understanding, usefulness, respect and next-step confidence—not only likelihood to recommend.

items.q: How is counsellor impact measured?
items.a: Review learner understanding, plan quality, action completion, safety and sustained progress while adjusting for case complexity. Avoid rewarding counsellors for steering users toward paid products.

items.q: How is internship impact measured?
items.a: Track access, selection fairness, completion, supervisor feedback, skill evidence, learner reflection, safety and subsequent opportunity. Job conversion is useful but not the only goal.

items.q: How is workshop impact measured?
items.a: Use objective-aligned pre/post evidence, observed practice and later action, alongside satisfaction. Report what changed and for whom.

items.q: Will impact reports be published?
items.a: Career Garage should publish periodic, privacy-safe reports with methods, sample sizes, limitations and both positive and negative findings. Independent review improves credibility.

items.q: How will feedback improve the platform?
items.a: Route feedback into named product, content, practitioner and safety owners; prioritise by severity and frequency; test changes; and close the loop with affected users.

items.q: What is the ultimate social impact?
items.a: The intended impact is greater career agency and fairer access to guidance, skills and opportunity—especially for learners excluded by geography, income, language or networks.

items.q: Why should anyone trust Career Garage?
items.a: Trust should be earned through transparent methods, verified people and partners, clear limits, strong privacy and safety, published evidence, accessible complaints and correction when the platform is wrong.

items.q: What evidence shows that the model works?
items.a: The model is plausible because it integrates established career-development components, but Career Garage-specific effectiveness must be demonstrated through pilots, validation and longitudinal outcomes. Do not substitute testimonials for evidence.

items.q: What if the assessments are inaccurate?
items.a: No assessment is error-free. Use multiple evidence sources, report uncertainty, allow retesting and human review, monitor bias and outcomes, and stop using any module that lacks adequate validity for its purpose.

items.q: What if AI reinforces social bias?
items.a: Measure subgroup performance, remove proxy variables where inappropriate, constrain use cases, include human review and appeals, document model changes and involve affected communities. If fairness cannot be established, do not automate the decision.  [R7]

items.q: What prevents Career Garage from becoming a course-selling funnel?
items.a: Separate guidance governance from commercial teams, disclose commissions, rank by suitability, show non-commercial alternatives, audit recommendations and never reward counsellors for sales.

items.q: What prevents employers from exploiting student data?
items.a: Default-deny access, explicit purpose and consent, contractual prohibitions, technical controls, audit logs, short retention, sanctions and no hidden assessment-data sharing.

items.q: How will Career Garage protect minors from unsafe adults?
items.a: Use verified adults, background checks where appropriate, no unrestricted adult–minor messaging, moderated channels, parental controls, conduct rules, rapid reporting, specialist response and law-enforcement escalation when required.  [R1–R2]

items.q: What happens if Career Garage gives a harmful recommendation?
items.a: Pause the affected workflow, provide human review and support, correct the record, notify impacted users where material, investigate root cause and publish governance improvements. Terms should not be used to avoid accountability.

items.q: Is Career Garage replacing parents, teachers or counsellors?
items.a: No. It gives each stakeholder better tools, information and coordination. Human relationships and contextual judgement remain central.

items.q: Is Career Garage trying to decide a child’s future?
items.a: No. It expands informed choice and encourages exploration. Its most important safeguard is refusing to convert a profile into a fixed destiny.

items.q: Why not use a free online career test?
items.a: A free test may be a useful prompt, but it rarely provides validated local interpretation, contextual counselling, an action plan, opportunities, safety and longitudinal support. Career Garage’s value must come from this connected quality—not the existence of a quiz.

items.q: Why pay when schools already have counsellors?
items.a: Career Garage can extend capacity with specialised assessments, content, opportunity networks, supervision and reporting. Where a school already has strong provision, the platform should complement it rather than duplicate services.

items.q: What is the biggest risk to the business?
items.a: The biggest risk is losing trust through overclaiming or inconsistent delivery. The response is staged scale, evidence gates, practitioner governance, child safety, data discipline and transparent correction.

items.q: What stops a competitor from copying the idea?
items.a: The concept can be copied; trusted execution is harder. Defensibility comes from validated tools, protected content, quality professionals, institutional workflows, safe opportunity networks, longitudinal data and a respected brand.

items.q: How will Career Garage remain independent?
items.a: Adopt conflict-of-interest rules, disclose revenue relationships, keep recommendation criteria separate from sales, diversify funding and establish external advisory oversight for assessment, ethics and safeguarding.

items.q: What approvals are required before launch?
items.a: Complete legal, privacy, consumer, tax, child-safety, assessment-IP, contracting and sector-specific review; obtain institution and partner approvals; and secure any licences triggered by actual services. Do not claim government approval unless formally granted.  [R1–R3, R9]

items.q: What has to be validated before public claims are made?
items.a: At minimum: assessment reliability and validity, norm samples, counsellor and mentor credentials, launch geography, language coverage, prices, partner counts, service levels, certificate status, opportunity volume, security controls and outcome claims.

items.q: Why is now the right time for Career Garage?
items.a: Learners face more pathways, faster skill change and unequal access to reliable guidance. India’s education direction also emphasises holistic development, career guidance, vocational exposure, internships and mentorship; Career Garage can serve that need if it earns trust through evidence and execution.  [R8]
